S26.02.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact, and one artifact with no title for the fallback check
S26.02.note: The fallback is Untitled plus the type (artifactPresentation.ts:79), not a fixed word; the viewer tab name is a slug of the title plus an extension, so it does not show the title verbatim.
steps: Sign in and make sure the account has at least one artifact.
Click More in the chat panel.
Click Artifacts. The list opens under the title Code, Artifacts.
Read the title on each row. Rows with no title should show Untitled followed by the type.
Open a row and compare the file name shown on the viewer tab with the title. The tab shows the title turned into a file name with an extension, not the title text itself.
S26.02.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then read the row title

S26.03.needs: a signed-in account with artifacts of different types
S26.03.note: The code only gives special icons to html, react, svg, mermaid and code; other types such as diagram, document or spreadsheet are shown as the raw type word from the server, with the generic file-code icon, and the code does not confirm those kinds exist.
steps: Sign in and make sure the account has artifacts of more than one type.
Click More in the chat panel, then click Artifacts.
Read the text after the icon on each row. The first word is the artifact type.
Open a row and look at the language shown in the status bar of the viewer.
Compare the type word and icon with Expected.
S26.03.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then read the row description

S26.05.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact
S26.05.note: No control to open an artifact was found in the chat webview, so the list is the only path from the UI; the palette command Code: Open Artifact takes an artifact id and no picker was found for it.
steps: Sign in and make sure the account has an artifact.
Click More in the chat panel, then click Artifacts.
Click an artifact row.
Look for a read-only text tab that shows the artifact content.
S26.05.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then click a row. The palette command is Code: Open Artifact

S26.06.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact
S26.06.note: The extension has no close command; closing is VS Code's own tab close. The row actions are copy, save into the workspace and open on web, and none deletes an artifact.
steps: Open an artifact from More > Artifacts.
Close its editor tab with the tab close button or Cmd+W.
Click More, then Artifacts again.
Look for the same row still in the list.
Click the row and check that the content opens again.
S26.06.where: Artifacts > click a row > close the viewer tab with its close button or Cmd+W

S26.07.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact; the reload step needs VS Code's Developer: Reload Window command
S26.07.note: No toggle was found; the list is loaded from the server index, so reopening after a reload works only while signed in.
steps: Open an artifact, then close its tab.
Click More, then Artifacts, and click the same row.
Run Developer: Reload Window from the Command Palette, then repeat the Artifacts step.
Compare the reopened content with the first view.
S26.07.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then click the same row again

S26.12.needs: a signed-in account with a conversation that has several artifacts
S26.12.note: Switching goes through the list picker, which closes after each pick; the viewer itself has no switch control, so the expectation of switching without leaving the viewer is not met by the code.
steps: Use a conversation with at least two artifacts.
Click More, then Artifacts, and click the first artifact.
Click More, then Artifacts again, and click the second artifact.
Compare the second content with the first and check that both can be opened.
S26.12.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then click a different row

labels.text: Opens read-only, re-derived from the message that produced it

S26.16.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact
S26.16.note: The read-only state comes from the document being served by a content provider; the code sets no explicit read-only flag, and no older-version or shared-copy read-only state was found.
steps: Sign in and open More, then Artifacts.
Hover a row and read its tooltip.
Click the row to open the artifact.
Try to type into the viewer tab.
Compare the tooltip and the viewer with Expected.
S26.16.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then hover a row

S26.30.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact
S26.30.note: The confirmation text is the product name, then copied and the title in quotes; the product name comes from a constant, so it is not a literal in the file.
steps: Open More, then Artifacts.
Hover the row of an artifact and click its copy icon, tooltip Copy the content.
Paste into any editor.
Compare the pasted text with the artifact content, and check for a confirmation message that says copied with the title.
S26.30.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then hover a row and click the Copy the content icon

S26.32.needs: a signed-in account with at least one published artifact and one unpublished artifact
S26.32.note: Only published artifacts get a label; an unpublished artifact shows no label, and the word private does not appear anywhere in the code. No publish control was found in VS Code.
steps: Sign in with an account that has a published artifact and one that is not published.
Click More, then Artifacts.
Read the end of each row description for the visibility words.
Hover a published row and read the tooltip explanation.
Compare the labels with Expected.
S26.32.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then read the row description
